title: Sons of Jacob: A Shadow of Things to Come

sense.text:
“But God shall shoot at them with an arrow; suddenly shall they be wounded. So they shall make their own tongue to fall upon themselves.” Their own tongue is the things they wrote in secret to pass amongst themselves. The Most High is revealing those things openly to his elect, to those who do their due diligence to search out the truths of the Bible: that the so-called blacks in America, the so-called Hispanics and natives, are the Israelites.

The upper echelon scholars have been passing these things around amongst themselves. Remember when they said if you want to hide something from a negro, put it in a book. The so-called white man never expected us to learn to read, never expected an Emancipation Proclamation, never expected the spirit of God to revive these dead bones so that we wake up and know who we are in these last days. So they put their secrets in their record books, and those books are being opened to us now, in correlation with the Bible: the Bible first and the primary source, everything else after it.

And their own records fall on them. During the Inquisition the black Jews were banished out of Spain and Portugal: King John II in 1492 sent them to the island of St. Thomas off the coast of West Africa, and from there we dwelt in Angola, Congo, Guinea and Senegambia. They are called the black Portuguese, the Jews of Loango. The Spanish Jews are the true descendants of the tribe of Judah and the royal house of David, scattered into the Iberian Peninsula from the time of Nebuchadnezzar. Those Jews were despised even by the hamitic tribes around them, and as persecuted communities they were more in danger of being raided by war parties of neighbouring Hamites and Ishmaelites and sold as slaves; many of them were among the slaves brought to America. The scholars are in agreement that the slaves brought to America were the royal lineage of King David.

The Ibn Yahya family traced their line through the exilarchs back to King David: treasurers to kings, mathematicians, astrologers, physicians, men of outstanding capability, just like the Israelites have always been when the Most High was with us, because he gave his word unto Jacob. Some of them bore the cognomen Negro: David Ibn Yahya Negro and Judah Ibn Yahya Negro. That sounds good coming off of Israelite lips. Ben means son of; our records were still intact and we knew whom we descended from.

The first Africans brought to Virginia in 1619 came out of Angola on the San Juan Bautista, a Spanish slave ship. In the census of 1624 to 1625 they are written down: Anthony Negro and Isabella Negro and William their child. The same name the Yahyas carried, out of the same lands they fled to. The ones who fled to Italy took the name Nero, black in Italian, and the slave records show the surname Nero disembarking in America at New Orleans. The royal house of David is here in America, thus saith the Lord, and that backs up Genesis 49 and the 12 tribes chart.

So we have no time to go back and forth debating Esau and these apologists, the modern day inquisitors. None of us should be confounded by pastors. Study, know your references, and be able to quote them.

“For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given”: unto us is possessive. Unto us, the children of Israel. The child that was born belonged to a particular nation of people.

“And the government shall be upon his shoulder”: the government means a body of people, and that body is Israel. It is rulership and dominion: Christ is going to rule, and we are going to be his government that sits upon his shoulder. Christ’s government pertains only to Israel. The world has a false illusion that Christ died for everybody and that when the kingdom of heaven is established it will be everybody holding hands. It will not.

“And his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.” These are the titles of Christ. He is the everlasting Father because he made all things: Christ is our father. He is the mighty God, and he is the Prince of Peace.

precepts.why:
“Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.” A virgin means a young woman of marriageable age. She shall conceive means she would have sex and get pregnant. Immanuel means God is with us.

“Butter and honey shall he eat, that he may know to refuse the evil, and choose the good”: the law of God would be in his mouth.

This is the child born unto us. He was given as a sign to a particular nation, so he belongs to that nation.

“And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.” His people is another possessive noun, basic English. That is the name of Christ: he saves the nation of Israel.

Why from our sins? Because some of the sins we could not repent for. Under the law, break the Sabbath and you were put to death; adultery, death; fornication, death; breaking the high holy days, death; idolatry, death. Through Christ we obtained the mercy to repent of those things.

“So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations; and from David until the carrying away into Babylon are fourteen generations; and from the carrying away into Babylon unto Christ are fourteen generations.” Babylon desecrated the temple too, not just Rome.

This shows we were always in captivity, and it did not stop with Christ. When Christ was on the earth, he was in captivity under the so-called white man, Rome, whom the Bible calls Esau. So the child born unto us was born to a captive nation, to save his people.

Why does the government sit upon his shoulder? A brother, Rodney, answered that Christ is coming back to save Jacob, Israel, and be governor over the nation, and that is part of it.

“He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David: And he shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever; and of his kingdom there shall be no end.” That is Christ. Everything shall be given unto him, and that is the government Isaiah is talking about: rulership, dominion. Christ is going to rule, and we are going to be his government that sits upon his shoulder.

“But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building.” Christ is the new high priest of good things to come.

The true scholars of the Bible say that government is only talking about Israel, and the high priest shows why. The ephod of the high priest has a stone for each tribe, three rows and four columns, as Soldier Moshe from Atlanta answered. The ephod is just for the tribes. Christ is the new high priest, representing the 12 tribes of Israel.

“And he put them on the shoulders of the ephod, that they should be stones for a memorial to the children of Israel; as the Lord commanded Moses.” What was on the high priest’s shoulder? Stones for a memorial to the children of Israel.

So what government is going to be upon the shoulder of Christ, the new high priest? Israel. “For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given”, and the government, Israel, shall be upon his shoulder.

“For the Lord is our judge, the Lord is our lawgiver, the Lord is our king; he will save us.” Where do you think America gets its so-called judicial system? From the Bible. The Lord is our judge: the judicial branch. The Lord is our lawgiver: the legislative branch. The Lord is our king: the executive branch.

But there will be no president, no terms, no four-year term and no coup. Christ is going to reign for ever and ever. The law comes out of Christ, and the executive branch out of the nation of Israel. That is the government upon his shoulder.

“Out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel”: that is the governor, Christ the ruler, the one the government is upon. “Whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting”: foretold of old by the prophets.

So why are we even having these debates? It is a waste of time. The Bible says what it says, and that is it.

This is for the title the everlasting Father. “I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.” Christ also has a Father, because he was created by the Most High God, and then Christ created us. Christ comes from God, and we come from Christ, literally.

“Philip saith unto him, Lord, shew us the Father, and it sufficeth us. Jesus saith unto him, Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip? he that hath seen me hath seen the Father.” Because Christ is the Father, our everlasting Father.
“I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending, saith the Lord, which is, and which was, and which is to come, the Almighty.” Just as Isaiah calls him the mighty God, Christ is that Almighty.

This explains the Prince of Peace. “For he is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us.” He is our peace.

Both one means back to one nation, the nation of Israel. The peace Christ brings is the joining of Israel back together as one.

sense.text:
Is there nepotism in the Bible? Yes. Nepotism is granting an advantage, privilege or position to relatives or friends. There are two kinds. There is the nigga nepotism, the evil kind: a man becomes mayor and fills every position with family and childhood friends who are unfit for it, solely because of the relationship. And there is the good nepotism: a licensed plumber opens Sons of Jacob Plumbing, raises his children fully trained to take over the family business, hires them, and when he passes they keep it going. That is the same thing Christ promised us. Christ who made us is giving the government, the kingdom, to Israel, his children, to those who deserve it.

“Lord, thy pound hath gained ten pounds.” These are the Israelites the Most High called, though some of them were not chosen. “Well, thou good servant: because thou hast been faithful in a very little, have thou authority over ten cities.” How did this Israelite gain authority over ten cities? By the things he did in his lifetime: his faith and his works, because his works proved his faith.

You did not have to beg that first brother to do the work. You did not have to beg him to travel, to get a passport and get his ass on a boat and go somewhere other than Oak Cliff or Grand Prairie, to fold a flyer, to keep the commandments, or to hazard his life. Christ hazarded his life for you Negroes. That is why every one of us woke up this morning. You think your heart is beating because of you? What the hell did you do? Nothing. We owe Christ.

“Lord, thy pound hath gained five pounds. And he said likewise to him, Be thou also over five cities.” This second brother was not as great as the first, but he still had works. Christ is handing out cities, handing out kingdoms, because these brothers proved themselves.

“Lord, behold, here is thy pound, which I have kept laid up in a napkin.” This brother did not do crap. He was a niggard, a sluggard, a sloth; he did nothing with what he was given. The little bit of wisdom Christ gives us, we are supposed to increase: cultivate it, plant seeds and watch it grow.

“Out of thine own mouth will I judge thee, thou wicked servant.” What is your excuse for not traveling? You are just lazy; you do not want to go nowhere. You are not the only one with a good job. Oh brother, my job: F your job. Nobody is saying quit your job. Take the time off in advance, the same way you take time off to take your wife somewhere for your anniversary, or whatever the hell you do. The travel is announced way in advance. Put the days you accumulate towards the Lord, and make the sacrifice for Christ the same way he made his sacrifice for you, for your simple behind, when none of us is worthy of the grace he gave. Some act like Christ owes them something.

“Thou knewest that I was an austere man.” We know Christ is austere because we read about it, and his Spirit was in the prophets, because they came from Christ the same way we come from Christ.

“Take from him the pound, and give it to him that hath ten pounds” … “That unto every one which hath shall be given; and from him that hath not, even that he hath shall be taken away from him.”

Just because we are Israelites does not mean a damn thing by itself. It is a great thing to be Israel, Romans 9 tells you about that, but we still have to put in the work to acquire a position in the kingdom of heaven and be lords over ten cities, over five cities. Do not listen to the camps that tell you that you can go around committing sins and still get the kingdom. Christ will take what he has given you and give it to another.

precepts.why:
Instances of nepotism in the scriptures, and it is only for Jacob and Sons. The so-called white people, the Ishmaelites and so-called Arabs who are watching and keeping the commandments: when Christ comes back you are going to be a slave, thus saith the Lord. That nepotism is only for us.

Joseph told Pharaoh, “My father and my brethren, and their flocks, and their herds, and all that they have, are come out of the land of Canaan”, and presented five of his brethren, who said, “Thy servants are shepherds, both we, and also our fathers.” Then “Joseph placed his father and his brethren, and gave them a possession in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.”

Joseph looked out for his brethren, his family, and gave them the best of the land. Pharaoh was not doing this for any other foreigners or nations. Joseph was allowed to do it because they were his next of kin.
“The name of the captain of his host was Abner, the son of Ner, Saul’s uncle.” Saul went to family first. When he needed a captain over his host, he hired his own uncle’s son, his kin.

“And Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the host.” King David appointed Joab commander of his army. Was Joab related to King David? Yes, as Chronicles shows. David’s offices were kept close: the host, the recorder, the priests and the scribe.

“And Jesse begat his firstborn Eliab” … “David the seventh: Whose sisters were Zeruiah, and Abigail. And the sons of Zeruiah; Abishai, and Joab, and Asahel, three.” Joab was the son of David’s sister: next of kin to King David.

So everything was kept in the family. It was seldom seen that we dealt with outsiders or other nations like that. The only time we dealt with them was when we needed them as servants, or when they were paying tribute.

“Now it came to pass, when the wall was built”: this is after Nehemiah built the walls that were torn down in the captivity of Babylon. “That I gave my brother Hanani, and Hananiah the ruler of the palace, charge over Jerusalem: for he was a faithful man, and feared God above many.”

He gave his brother charge over Jerusalem because he was a faithful man, just like the brother with the pounds whom Christ made lord over ten cities. You do not give a relative charge over your business unless he is faithful, and that is the same thing Christ is demanding of the children of Jacob. We have to be faithful if we want that kingdom.

And he “feared God above many”: that is the key. He was not doing anything in the dark. Those still walking in sin in the dark, repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand, or you will be given charge over nothing but the everlasting fire. In the times of our forefathers, dealing with your next of kin and your nation was highly preferred. Modern Christianity under white supremacy gives the false illusion of a non-hierarchical government in Christ’s kingdom.

Our forefathers preferred their next of kin, and so should we, if the brother is in his right mind and can get the job done. Brothers have hired brothers and had their business ruined. We are all coming out of a low estate, so examine the brother or sister before you bring them on board, the same way Christ is going to examine us.

“Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another; Not slothful in business; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord.” If a brother is slothful you are not going to prefer him over anything. The Lord wants you fervent, on fire for this truth, not a little smoke; he does not want a man or a woman of excuses.

The same way our forefathers preferred one another, Christ prefers us, because we come out of Christ. Who better to give everything to than your children? That is what the other nations and the apologists do not understand. But we cannot be slothful, and we have to be fervent. We are not at our rest; we have to usher in the second coming of Christ by teaching his laws and waking up the dead of our people, so the Most High will seal them and bring in the 144.

sense.text:
If we are supposed to prefer one another, how much more is Christ going to prefer us, since we are part of the body of Christ? “Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?” We are the temple of God, literally.

The Spirit of God dwells in us when we are keeping the commandments of God. When we are not keeping the commandments, we are the children of the devil.

“If any man defile the temple of God, him shall God destroy; for the temple of God is holy, which temple ye are.” If you defile yourselves with drugs, pornography, prostitution and wickedness, God says him shall he destroy.

precepts.why:
“What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own?” Our body is the temple of the Holy Ghost, and we are not our own. A lot of us walk around as if Christ owes us. Our body is not ours.

So do not walk around getting tattoos; many of us did in the world, but repent of it when you come into the truth. Drugs, crack, coke, alcohol, and food too, because food is a drug: it is time to lose the weight. The brothers have to be the example first, and then the sisters are getting in place too: burning the fat, no more walking through the doorways sideways.

“For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God’s.” How do we glorify God in our bodies? The body is just a vehicle, a vessel. What we do with it is what the Most High is interested in, and that is keeping the commandments.

“Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.” The Jews got simple: “Forty and six years was this temple in building, and wilt thou rear it up in three days?” They thought he meant the literal temple. “But he spake of the temple of his body.”

So Christ’s body is the temple, and now we are the temple of God, because we come from Christ.

sense.text: “Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God.” This is not talking about the heathens. It is talking about the Israelites who were scattered, the northern kingdom and the remnants of the Jews, who were scattered and were living like heathens.
“Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone”: Christ is the chief corner stone of this building.

“In whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord.” Fitly framed together is Israel with no schisms in the body. Everybody is supposed to come together and fall in line, like Voltron: no divisions, no strife, malice or guile in the body. Just like the temple Solomon built.

“In whom ye also are builded together for an habitation of God through the Spirit.” This is talking about the chosen. Builded together means you cannot do it without each other and you cannot do it on your own. We need each other. The pinky needs the thumb; take any limb away and the others have to compensate. So we have to move in the spirit, because we depend on each other.

precepts.why:
“And the house, when it was in building, was built of stone made ready before it was brought thither: so that there was neither hammer nor axe nor any tool of iron heard in the house, while it was in building.” When Solomon built the temple it was glorious and beautiful, fitly framed together. It was dovetailing: the stones were cut to fit like a puzzle piece or a Lego, so you did not need a nail to fasten it or anything to constrain it. That is how the wise man King Solomon built the temple.

That is the same way we should be coming together, with no issues. We are coming out of the world, so we know there are going to be issues, but over time we have to get it right and do better.

“For we are members of his body, of his flesh, and of his bones.” Literally: Christ took a piece of himself and made us, as the Bishop brought out. We are literally from Christ, and that is why we are supposed to be Christlike.

That is one of the reasons the kingdom is going to be given unto his chosen. We are from him; he is not giving it to anybody who is not his children. That is perfect nepotism, beautiful nepotism.

That is why the heathens are in an uproar and grab their Great White Hope to come challenge the Israelites, as if prophecy will not be fulfilled. That is how you know they are atheists: everywhere in the scriptures it is about Israel, and in the book of Revelation, who gets the kingdom? Israel. Their debates and YouTube views will not change anything. Even if they put us to death, the kingdom will be given to the Israelites.

This further shows what Ephesians 5 says, that we are members of his body. “I pray for them: I pray not for the world, but for them which thou hast given me; for they are thine.” He did not pray for the Moabites or the Ammonites. Christians read this and do not comprehend it.

“And all mine are thine, and thine are mine”: Christ is talking to the Most High. “That they may be one, as we are”: Christ is one with the Father because he came from the Father, and we are one in him because we come from him.

“Those that thou gavest me I have kept, and none of them is lost, but the son of perdition”: that is Judas, that the scripture might be fulfilled. Those that were given to Christ are back here today, on this earth.

“The world hath hated them, because they are not of the world, even as I am not of the world.” We are hated the same way today: you see the videos saying those are not Israelites, they are just blacks who want an identity, the laws of God are done away with. “They are not of the world, even as I am not of the world.” We are not of this world, brothers.

“And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he might have the preeminence.” Christ is the head of the body, the church. In all things Christ will have the preeminence; that is why he is the Lord of lords and the King of kings. He is the chief corner stone the building rests on.

“For as we have many members in one body, and all members have not the same office: So we, being many, are one body in Christ, and every one members one of another.” We are one body in Christ because we come from Christ.

Members one of another, because we depend on one another, and we are all related: we come from the same nation, some of us from the same tribes. That is why we are told to prefer one another in all things.

“For as the body is one, and hath many members, and all the members of that one body, being many, are one body: so also is Christ.” We are part of Christ, and Christ is part of us. That is the building fitly framed together.

sense.text:
“But to us there is but one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we in him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him.” By whom are all things: principalities, everything you see on the earth and in the heavens, the sun, the moon and the stars. Christ created everything, even us. “And we by him”, because Christ our Father created us.

He created everything, but he prefers Israel.

precepts.why: “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” That is Christ. “All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.” All things were made by Christ: the one Lord by whom are all things.

“For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible.” The sun, moon, stars and planets, everything on earth, and things you cannot see with the naked eye: all created by Jesus Christ, our Father, our Messiah, our God. “Whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him.”

That is why he is going to put everything under his feet: it belonged to him in the first place. And we, being heirs with Christ, he is going to give those things to us, if we are faithful and fervent. That is the only way we are going to get it.

“And he is before all things, and by him all things consist.” That is why he is the Alpha and Omega.

“Hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds.” When Christ was on the scene, that was considered the last days; the last days started then.

Christ made the worlds, meaning he made everything. He was before the beginning, and he made the beginning you read about in Genesis. He is the heir of all things, and he prefers the nation of Israel: the so-called blacks, Hispanics and natives, those of slave descent, of Israelite descent.

“Hear this word that the Lord hath spoken against you, O children of Israel, against the whole family which I brought up from the land of Egypt, saying, You only have I known of all the families of the earth.” Plain and simple. Nothing changed in the New Testament. He created everybody, but he only knew Israel: he had that special relationship with Israel, he preferred Israel.

“Therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities.” That is why the royal line of David was taken into captivity. The slave ships existed because of iniquity, and the prison system exists because of iniquity, because we are in sin. Now it is time to come up out of that sin.

sense.text:
One of the favourite scriptures, like a punch in the stomach. “And ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel”: a father in the midst of his children. The Father is not going to neglect us and walk away. The Most High did not forget about his children; the shepherd did not forget about his sheep.

“And that I am the Lord your God, and none else.” Possessive: I am the Lord your God. How plain. Translate it into any language and it is the same. This Bible is not all-inclusive; it is exclusive to the Israelites. People are lost because they hate God and cannot see themselves prosper without holding on to the wrists of the so-called white man.

The mind is so calcified with the doctrine of Christianity that when it hears this, it bothers it; it cannot seep into the deep recesses of the mind. If the butter cannot marinate on that biscuit, God tosses it in the garbage, and that garbage is going to be on fire. The yoke of Christianity and of the so-called white man has you saying you do not have to keep the commandments, following the holidays of men and man-made religion. All of these things were created when we were destroyed as a people. Even after the yokes of iron came off it was still slavery: the Black Codes, the Code Noir in the islands, the Jim Crow laws, sharecropping. It is 2025 and we are still confused as a people. When are we going to turn back to the God who made us?

“And my people shall never be ashamed.” But you will be put to shame if you are not studying. Go up against a pastor unstudied and he will record your ass, upload it, and you will be confounded and your face will wax pale. Nobody in purple and gold should be getting confounded by any pork chop eating pastor, black, white or Asian; I don’t give a damn. This is the true institution of biblical scholars, Israel United in Christ.

precepts.why:
We read Hosea 5:15, that he left and returned to his place. But right after that, once we repent: “Come, and let us return unto the Lord.” He returned to his place, so now we have to go after him and seek him, because we backslid, moonwalking away from the Most High God.

“For he hath torn, and he will heal us.” He tore us apart in slavery. The yokes of iron came off, but we were bugged out of our minds with religion, doctrine, philosophy and the ideology of men. “He hath smitten, and he will bind us up.” He has already started that process. That is why we are here getting our minds right, why we no longer call ourselves Jamaicans, Haitians or American blacks, why we no longer carry the last names Robinson, Patterson or Jean-Claude. We surnamed ourselves Israel, because that is what the Bible says, and we know who we are now.

That is the Father in the midst of Israel.

sense.text:
Paul is speaking: “Who are Israelites; to whom pertaineth” All of this is possessive, still speaking about the same people.

“The adoption”: Christ adopting us into the covenant, the New Covenant, dying for the nation of Israel, as Matthew 1:21 says, he shall save his people, not everyone else.

“And the glory”: the kingdom of heaven, being exalted amongst all nations on this planet, pertains only to the Israelites.

“And the covenants”, plural. The old covenant belonged to Israel, plain and simple, and Hebrews 8:8 tells you the New Covenant belongs to Israel only. “And the giving of the law”: the law was only given to the Israelites. “And the service of God”: given to the Levites, and eventually to all Israel, because we are all kings and priests. “And the promises”: those pertain to Israel too. This whole chapter is talking about Israel.

“Whose are the fathers”: Abraham. Abraham had many children, but who received the promise after him? Isaac. Isaac had two boys, and the promise went to Jacob. Jacob had 12 boys who received the promise, and we are the children of Jacob today: Jacob and Sons, never to be diminished, only replenished when Christ returns.

“And of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came”: Christ came out of an Israelite. “Who is over all, God blessed for ever. Amen.” Although we are living out these curses, they have an end. When Christ comes back there shall be no more curse, as Revelation says. But we have to do our due diligence in keeping God’s laws and teaching his word; we have to be faithful men, and fervent.

“For I have given you an example, that ye should do as I have done to you.” You cannot open the Bible and say you do not know how to live. Christ gave us the example. Although we have sinned, we have to sin less, because Christ gave the perfect example of how to walk.

That is how you know Christianity is garbage. You cannot even throw it in your local garbage dump, because the damn Christian will run and grab whatever you threw away and put it back in his mind; you have to burn it and watch it disintegrate. Christ said he left an example. Did Christ keep Tabernacles? Yes. The feast of dedication? Yes. Did Christ have fringes, the hem of his garment? Yes. So why are the apologists, these pathetic modern day inquisitors, not doing it? They do not believe in Christ. They believe in the so-called white man, the devil. They are atheists holding the Bible, posing as believers.
“Verily, verily, I say unto you”: verily means seriously. “Before Abraham was, I am.” Christ was always in the beginning. This is brought out because Abraham is coming next: Abraham came from Christ.

“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” The scriptures are what give us true comfort. Whatever we are going through, our forefathers went through the same thing, if not worse. Sickness: our forefathers were sick and were healed. Loss of a job, of wealth, of assets: look at Job. There is nothing we cannot overcome.

But to understand what was written aforetime, you have to study. You have to actually open the book and read. Your mind has to be in this book; your life has to be submerged in the water of God, which is his word.

Christ made us, and we are part of Christ. So there are things that happened in the lives of our forefathers that were echoed in the life of Christ: a shadow of things to come in Christ, because Christ is in us and we are part of Christ. This is the forefather Abraham.

“Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father’s house, unto a land that I will shew thee.” This was in Chaldea. Unto a land that I will shew thee means Abraham never saw that land before, but because he had faith he believed on the word of God.

What makes it worse: some of us have seen the islands on TV and seen videos of Africa, some even visited while in the world, but now in the truth will not step one foot outside of this state called Texas. How great is your faith? It is less than a mustard seed; you cannot even see it with the damn telescope, that is how tiny it is. Abraham, who had not seen the land, was moved with faith to believe on God. Israel is scattered in all nations and the work has to be done there, but we have to beg you to travel. It is time to grow.

“And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee.” That is why the Most High is going to curse these nations: they have been cursing us until this very day. Look what Trump is doing: taking our brothers of the northern kingdom and deporting them, but not doing that to the Ukrainians, the Amalekites who came over. They still hate our guts. We praise the Most High, because prophecy is being fulfilled, and we want to usher in the second coming of Christ; hell breaking loose is the only way our people are going to wake up.

“And in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.” Who is going to be blessed? Israel. And who is the thee? Christ.

“So Abram departed, as the Lord had spoken unto him.” He had faith and he departed; he did what God asked him. God speaks to us through the Bible, so why are we not listening? We have brothers and sisters in other countries depending on us. Where is your passport? Collecting dust at home, or you do not even have one. You do not want to leave because you are comfortable in Babylon. You do not have faith.

precepts.why:
“Ye are the children of the prophets, and of the covenant which God made with our fathers, saying unto Abraham, And in thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed.” The seed is Christ, the thee of Genesis 12:3.

“Unto you first God, having raised up his Son Jesus, sent him to bless you, in turning away every one of you from his iniquities.” We are blessed because of Christ; we are here because of Christ. We cannot roll with the spirit that Christ owes us something. We owe Christ.

That is how we are blessed and how we are going to get the kingdom: only through Christ, only through the blood of the Lamb, not because of anything you think you have done or will do. The works are expected, because they are our reasonable service, but there is nothing we can do in this body to repay Christ, because we are all wicked as hell, a wicked nation of people who transgress God’s laws day in and day out.

Abraham showed a consistent pattern of faith. “Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them: and he said unto him, So shall thy seed be. And he believed in the Lord.” That is why God blessed him: he believed.

The Most High knows the counsels of men; he knows whether you are full of it or whether you believe. Abraham believed, “and he counted it to him for righteousness.”

sense.text: “God did tempt Abraham” … “Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac, whom thou lovest” … “and offer him there for a burnt offering upon one of the mountains which I will tell thee of.” His only son.
“And Abraham rose up early in the morning, and saddled his ass.” Did he hesitate? No. He rose up early in the morning, clave the wood, and went unto the place God had told him of.

“Behold the fire and the wood: but where is the lamb for a burnt offering?” Put yourself in that situation. Think how great Abraham’s faith was, to go to sacrifice his son with no hesitation: not doubting himself, not questioning himself, not questioning God, doing what God said. Instant obedience to instructions. That is the level we have to bring our faith and our obedience to.

“My son, God will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering.” He bound Isaac, laid him on the altar, and “took the knife to slay his son.”

“For now I know that thou fearest God, seeing thou hast not withheld thy son, thine only son from me.” For now I know: in verse 1 God tempted Abraham, and through his actions, through the level of his faith, now God knows, although he already knew. Then the ram caught in a thicket was offered in his stead.

We see through the forefather Abraham that he had great faith. Abraham came from Christ, and that great faith was also in Christ: a shadow of things to come. What is in the father is in the son, and we are the sons of the father, so that same faith has to be in us.

precepts.why:
Abraham was tempted; so was Christ. “Then was Jesus led up of the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted of the devil.” After forty days of fasting the tempter said, “command that these stones be made bread”, and Christ answered, “It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.” That is faith: depending on the word.

Notice he quoted scriptures. On the pinnacle of the temple: “It is written again, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.” On the exceeding high mountain, offered all the kingdoms of the world: “Get thee hence, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.”

Look at the level of Christ’s faith in the Most High God: he recited scripture to ward off Satan and did not give in to the temptations.

This was the raising of Lazarus. “Father, I thank thee that thou hast heard me. And I knew that thou hearest me always: but because of the people which stand by I said it, that they may believe that thou hast sent me.” He gave all glory to the Father, so the people standing by, whose faith was little, could hear him praising the Father and believe that he is the Messiah. Then “Lazarus, come forth.”

Although Christ was a God, with principalities and powers and all things made by him, he still gave glory to the Father and still had faith in his Father, the same way we are supposed to have faith in Christ, our Father. That is why we started with John 8:58: Abraham had faith in Christ. It was Christ who was commanding Abraham.

“Good Master, what good thing shall I do, that I may have eternal life? And he said unto him, Why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, that is, God.” Was Christ good? He was more than excellent; he was without sin, perfect. Yet he took all the glory off of himself and gave it to the Father. That is faith in the Father.

“Pray that ye enter not into temptation”, he told the disciples. Then he withdrew “about a stone’s cast, and kneeled down, and prayed, Saying, Father, if thou be willing, remove this cup from me: nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done.”

Christ submitted to God’s will, trusting in the Father’s plan that he would lay down his life for the children of Israel, as Abraham did not withhold his only son.

If Christ was God and knew all things and had all this power, why was it like that? “For verily he took not on him the nature of angels; but he took on him the seed of Abraham. Wherefore in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren.” Made like his brethren: the same emotions and feelings, everything we experience, that fear. That is why he said, Father, take this cup from me, but he knew the will had to be done and that it was necessary to come and die for his children, the nation of Israel.

“That he might be a merciful and faithful high priest in things pertaining to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people. For in that he himself hath suffered being tempted, he is able to succour them that are tempted.” He had to understand what we go through, so he put his temple through the same thing. He went through it, overcame and was perfect, so he is able to comfort us when we are tempted.

So Abraham had great faith because Christ was in him, and Christ is in us, because we are his children.

sense.text: Now the forefather Joseph. “Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age: and he made him a coat of many colours.” Israel is Jacob. “They hated him, and could not speak peaceably unto him.”

They hated him for many reasons: because Jacob loved him the most, and because he had these dreams and could interpret them. “My sheaf arose, and also stood upright; and, behold, your sheaves stood round about, and made obeisance to my sheaf.” Imagine: your brothers do not even like you, and now you tell them this dream.

“Shalt thou indeed reign over us? or shalt thou indeed have dominion over us?” As if, this dude wants to be the head in charge. “And they hated him yet the more for his dreams, and for his words.” Joseph was hated by his own blood brothers. Write these scriptures down to see the parallel: a shadow of things to come.

precepts.why:
“Is not this the carpenter’s son? is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas? And his sisters, are they not all with us? Whence then hath this man all these things?” All these things are the wisdom he spoke in the synagogue in verse 54. “And they were offended in him”: his own brothers, his own cousins of Judah, Benjamin and Levi.

“A prophet is not without honour, save in his own country, and in his own house.” That is why there is the saying familiarity breeds contempt. They knew him and hated him.

This is talking about the Jews, not the rest of the tribes. When it says he came unto his own and his own received him not, the own are the elders, scribes and Pharisees of his own kinship, not the whole nation of Israel; the disciples were Israelites and they received him. That is why the Christian church is so stuck on stupid about “his own”. The doctrine of Christianity is wrong: false, damn lies. Christ was hated amongst his kin, just like Joseph.

“After these things Jesus walked in Galilee: for he would not walk in Jewry, because the Jews sought to kill him.” His brethren told him, “Depart hence, and go into Judea” … “shew thyself to the world. For neither did his brethren believe in him.”

His own brethren did not believe on Christ. It is the same with Joseph: Joseph’s brothers did not believe on him, and they conspired to kill him. Christ’s own kin, the scribes and Pharisees, did not believe on him either.

sense.text: “And when they saw him afar off, even before he came near unto them, they conspired against him to slay him.” Before he even came to them, they were conspiring to kill Joseph. That is wicked. “Behold, this dreamer cometh.” Put yourself back there: the youngest one, with all these dreams of us paying homage to him. Look at this damn dreamer. Keep it quiet; we want to kill him.

precepts.why:
“Then assembled together the chief priests, and the scribes, and the elders of the people, unto the palace of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas, And consulted that they might take Jesus by subtilty, and kill him.” They wanted to take him by subtilty because they knew he was innocent.

It was no knee-jerk, last-minute thing. It was always in the making: the priests, the chief men and the elders conspiring to kill our Lord and Saviour, because they hated him, the same as Joseph’s brethren conspired before he came near.

The same thing Christ went through, we are going to go through, if Christ is in us. “Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name’s sake.”

What threat does Christianity as it is taught today pose to the United Snakes of America, Babylon the great? None at all: it is all-inclusive, democracy, a white man Jesus. But a black Jesus coming through the sky to invade this place and enslave all nations, they call that treason. Those who teach the Bible and are Christlike, his children, the sons of Jacob, will be killed because of what we teach and do: keeping the commandments of God, going against what society reverences, getting our people off Christmas and Easter and keeping their money in their pockets. On a mass level that brings down the economy and empties their churches, and the modern day inquisitors will go to the heathen and complain, to kill us. Hated of all nations: Moab, Ammon, Ishmael, Esau, Ham. If we were teaching everybody to love Jesus, holding hands, laws done away with, what threat would that be? This shows that Christianity and all its denominations are a joke: trash, garbage, filth, dung.

“And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.” That is the familiars. Some are sitting in here to spy out, and they will conspire with Esau to come against us. It is written, so it is going to be fulfilled one way or the other.

sense.text: Just as Joseph’s kin conspired against him, the same happened to Christ. “And Judah said unto his brethren, What profit is it if we slay our brother, and conceal his blood? Come, and let us sell him to the Ishmeelites.” Judah! Do not get mad: this is coming from one of the only Levites in the congregation, outnumbered, and we all come out of the waters of Judah. “For he is our brother and our flesh.”

They “sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver: and they brought Joseph into Egypt.” They sold him to the Arabs, for silver. Which tribe sold him? Judah conspired to sell his brother.

precepts.why:
“Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went unto the chief priests, And said unto them, What will ye give me, and I will deliver him unto you? And they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver.” What does the name Judas mean? Judas in Greek is Judah.

Judah conspired to sell Joseph for silver; Judas sold Christ for silver. “And from that time he sought opportunity to betray him.” The same way Joseph was sold into slavery and betrayed by his brother, Judas betrayed Christ.

Prophecy had to be fulfilled, even with Judah and his brothers selling Joseph. The Most High did that for a reason: so they might be saved later in the time of famine, because of the level Joseph rose to in Egypt.

“And I took the thirty pieces of silver, and cast them to the potter in the house of the Lord.” That is prophecy fulfilled through Judas’s betrayal of Christ. It had to happen that way.

sense.text: “The Hebrew servant, which thou hast brought unto us, came in unto me to mock me.” His master’s wrath was kindled and he put Joseph “into the prison, a place where the king’s prisoners were bound.” Joseph was falsely accused.
“But the Lord was with Joseph, and shewed him mercy, and gave him favour in the sight of the keeper of the prison.”

precepts.why:
“And the chief priests and all the council sought for witness against Jesus to put him to death; and found none. For many bare false witness against him, but their witness agreed not together.” They sought witnesses and found none, so they bore false witness: “We heard him say, I will destroy this temple that is made with hands, and within three days I will build another made without hands.”

They falsely accused Christ, the same thing that happened to Joseph.

sense.text: “And the captain of the guard charged Joseph with them.” These are Joseph’s fellow prisoners, “the butler and the baker of the king of Egypt, which were bound in the prison.” Two men were imprisoned with Joseph.

precepts.why: “Then were there two thieves crucified with him, one on the right hand, and another on the left.” Two were with Christ, as two were bound with Joseph. And as with Joseph, one was spared: the butler was spared and the other was put to death. The same thing happened in its time with the two thieves.

Both men died with Christ, but one inherited eternal life. One railed on him: “If thou be Christ, save thyself and us.” The other rebuked him: “Dost not thou fear God” … “we receive the due reward of our deeds: but this man hath done nothing amiss.” And he said, “Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.” “To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.”

He was spared. Although his flesh died, his spirit lived on and he was in paradise with Christ, because he repented. The other big mouth idiot did not inherit anything, because he was not a believer and did not repent.

sense.text: “There is none so discreet and wise as thou art: Thou shalt be over my house, and according unto thy word shall all my people be ruled: only in the throne will I be greater than thou” … “See, I have set thee over all the land of Egypt.” Joseph became an exalted servant, second to Pharaoh over all of Egypt. After a period of time, he was exalted.

precepts.why:
“He humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross. Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name.” This is Christ. He is exalted the same way: as everyone in Egypt obeyed Joseph’s word, everybody is going to obey his word.

“That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth.” All nations are going to bow down, and even the angels are going to bow, “And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.”

sense.text:
“There stood no man with him, while Joseph made himself known unto his brethren. And he wept aloud” … “I am Joseph; doth my father yet live? And his brethren could not answer him; for they were troubled at his presence.” “I am Joseph your brother, whom ye sold into Egypt. Now therefore be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves” … “for God did send me before you to preserve life.”

When the brothers first came, they could not tell whether it was Joseph, because Joseph looked like the Egyptians: not only was he black, but he was dressed in the garments of the ancient Egyptians. The second time is when they knew him, because Joseph revealed himself to them.

“And he fell upon his brother Benjamin’s neck, and wept; and Benjamin wept upon his neck.” The second coming of Joseph is when the brothers realized who he was, and they wept, because they understood the wrong they had done.

precepts.why:
“And they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son.” When Christ comes back, we are going to mourn for him, because we are going to recognize the wrongs we did.

The first time Christ was on the scene there were so many unbelievers who did not recognize him. But when he comes again the whole world is going to know that is Jesus Christ, because of the way he comes back: it is unheard of. Not only are his hands pierced. Just as Joseph’s brethren knew him the second time and wept.

“Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel? And he said unto them, It is not for you to know the times or the seasons, which the Father hath put in his own power.”

“Ye men of Galilee, why stand ye gazing up into heaven? this same Jesus, which is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven.” This same Jesus, this black man Jesus. There will be no confusion when Christ comes back: a black man with woolly hair and pierced hands, coming out of that chariot. In the second coming you are going to know exactly who he is, and then, as Zechariah 12 says, we will weep for him, the same as Joseph’s brothers.

sense.text:
Now the forefather Nehemiah. “O Lord, I beseech thee, let now thine ear be attentive to the prayer of thy servant” … “For I was the king’s cupbearer.” What is a cupbearer? A brother answered that he carried the king’s chalice and presented the wine. And he had to take a sip of whatever the king drank, to make sure there was no poison in it. If he drank it and dropped dead, the king knew there was poison. He took that responsibility.

To be the king’s cupbearer, Nehemiah had to be willing to die for the king if necessary.

precepts.why: “And it came to pass in the month Nisan, in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes the king, that wine was before him: and I took up the wine, and gave it unto the king.” He was the king’s cupbearer, serving the king his wine.

Like Nehemiah, Christ dwelt at the right hand of the Father and was willing to drink the cup the Father had for him, even though it meant his death. “O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt.”

So Christ drank of that cup. Christ was the cupbearer to the King, the Father, and he had to drink that cup the same way Nehemiah had to.

“Grant that these my two sons may sit, the one on thy right hand, and the other on the left, in thy kingdom. But Jesus answered and said, Ye know not what ye ask. Are ye able to drink of the cup that I shall drink of” … “They say unto him, We are able.”

Some of us, not all of us, are going to have to drink of that same cup. There is no escaping it. That cup is death and persecution, the same thing Christ went through.

sense.text: “Why is thy countenance sad, seeing thou art not sick? this is nothing else but sorrow of heart” … “why should not my countenance be sad, when the city, the place of my fathers’ sepulchres, lieth waste, and the gates thereof are consumed with fire?” Nehemiah was in great anguish and pain over the destruction of the temple and the walls.

“That thou wouldest send me unto Judah, unto the city of my fathers’ sepulchres, that I may build it.” Being the king’s cupbearer was a high estate, a high position. But his people were on his mind: the estate of Israel was greater to him than his own estate, so he returned to Jerusalem to build the walls.

precepts.why:
“He that sendeth forth light, and it goeth, calleth it again, and it obeyeth him with fear. The stars shined in their watches, and rejoiced: when he calleth them, they say, Here we be.” This is Christ. “This is our God, and there shall none other be accounted of in comparison of him” “He hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved.”

He was at a high estate, because he was in the beginning; that is why he is the Alpha and Omega. “Afterward did he shew himself upon earth, and conversed with men.” That is when he brought himself to a low estate as man, because it behoved him to be made like his brethren, so he could take on our afflictions and die for us.

The same way Nehemiah left his great estate because the condition of his people mattered more than himself, Christ left the heavens and came down manifest in the flesh to die for the nation of Israel.

sense.text: “Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, and Geshem the Arabian” … “laughed us to scorn, and despised us, and said, What is this thing that ye do? will ye rebel against the king?” This is the opposition Nehemiah faced rebuilding God’s walls.

“The God of heaven, he will prosper us; therefore we his servants will arise and build: but ye have no portion, nor right, nor memorial, in Jerusalem.” That is hard, all praises to the Most High for it. The same thing Nehemiah said is what we need to say today. Christ echoed the same thing with the woman who wanted the blessing for her daughter: he told her no, and only when she answered that even the dogs eat of the crumbs from the master’s table was her daughter healed.

“And you, being dead in your sins” … “hath he quickened together with him, having forgiven you all trespasses.” The first enemy Christ overcame is sin. Now we have a chance to repent of our sins because of Christ.

“Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us.” The handwriting of ordinances that was against us is the law of animal sacrifice, which would not make us perfect. There were things we could not sacrifice for; his own blood and flesh had to be sacrificed. “And took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross.”

precepts.why:
“Knowing this, that our old man is crucified with him, that the body of sin might be destroyed, that henceforth we should not serve sin.” We are not supposed to serve sin in the body. That is the first enemy Christ got rid of.

The second, when he comes back, is the literal enemy: the devil, the so-called white man, and all the heathens.

sense.text: Just as Christ re-established the covenant and reinforced the law, Nehemiah did the same thing. “All the people gathered themselves together as one man” … “and they spake unto Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the law of Moses, which the Lord had commanded to Israel.” Ezra read it from the morning until midday, “and the ears of all the people were attentive unto the book of the law.”

precepts.why: “Thou camest down also upon mount Sinai, and spakest with them from heaven, and gavest them right judgments, and true laws, good statutes and commandments.” Nehemiah was enforcing God’s laws. After they built the wall, he and Ezra started to establish God’s laws again, because we had started to forget the covenant and the laws, the same way we had forgotten the feast of tabernacles.
“From the time that I was appointed to be their governor in the land of Judah” … “that is, twelve years.” For 12 years Nehemiah was the governor of Israel, ruling over us and teaching us God’s laws.
“What good thing shall I do, that I may have eternal life?” … “if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments.” Christ enforced the commandments, as Nehemiah did.

“Except your righteousness shall exceed the righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees, ye shall in no case enter into the kingdom of heaven. Ye have heard that it was said by them of old time, Thou shalt not kill.”

Christ magnified the law. Thou shalt not kill, but even hating your brother is a form of killing. Then adultery: even to look upon a woman and lust after her is the start of adultery. Christ reinforced and magnified God’s laws, and what Christ did was inside of Nehemiah.

sense.text: “Eliashib the priest, having the oversight of the chamber of the house of our God, was allied unto Tobiah: And he had prepared for him a great chamber” … “But in all this time was not I at Jerusalem.” After the 12 years, Nehemiah returned to the king to serve him, and during that time sin started to increase. Tobiah was sleeping in the temple; he turned the temple into his home like a bum.

“And it grieved me sore: therefore I cast forth all the household stuff of Tobiah out of the chamber.” In the same chapter we started marrying heathenish wives, and Nehemiah went around smacking us up to correct us.

When did he lay hands on people and drag Tobiah out of the temple? Not the first time; the second time. The second coming of Nehemiah. The same with Christ: the second coming of Christ is judgment and destruction. No long talking, no pleading, no conversations: swift judgment.

precepts.why: “I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and will plead with them there for my people and for my heritage Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations, and parted my land.” That is the swift judgment of the second coming.

“As thou didst rejoice at the inheritance of the house of Israel, because it was desolate, so will I do unto thee: thou shalt be desolate, O mount Seir, and all Idumea, even all of it.” That is Esau, Idumea, the so-called white man. All the Caucasians are going to be desolate, all the lands they possess. “And they shall know that I am the Lord.”

“Surely in the fire of my jealousy have I spoken against the residue of the heathen, and against all Idumea, which have appointed my land into their possession with the joy of all their heart, with despiteful minds, to cast it out for a prey.” All Idumea: that is the USA and all the Caucasian countries.

“For I will gather all nations against Jerusalem to battle; and the city shall be taken, and the houses rifled, and the women ravished.” That is talking about destruction. The women ravished is not us doing that; the other nations will be doing it.

“Then shall the Lord go forth, and fight against those nations, as when he fought in the day of battle.” Christ is going to fight against all nations that put their hand on the nation of Israel. Then we are going to rule with Christ, and the government will be given unto his sons. Jacob and Sons shall continue.
